High end Vietnamese food
Sep 2022 • Couples
Recommended by hotel concierge upon checking in. 10 mins walk form Meliá Hanoi and find this traditional Vietnamese food. Is is definitely an upper class Vietnamese food for sure but the quality is guaranteed! Love the pomelo salad as I always look forward it. The fried squid looks like chrysanthemum flower rather bland inside but with the special prepared dipping sauce , pretty good. The grilled chicken thigh with fried rice cake! Rather bland for the chicken meat for sure and need more marination ! The rice cake is great and brought me back to my nostalgia time that my grandma prepared for us ! The decor is very traditional Vietnamese setting and service is great..!

Elegant beautiful place, food good but not outstanding
Mar 2018 • Couples
From the outside you can tell this is an elegant, sophisticated restaurant. We were surprised when we looked at the menu prior to going in that the prices were lower than we would have expected at such a nice place. We felt underdressed and would definitely think about changing to a bit nicer attire before going in. The interior is even nicer than the outside. We were brought a bowl of those little rice crackers and spicy sauce when we sat down, which has been unheard of at any other restaurant in Vietnam or Thailand we visited on this trip. We ordered lemongrass chili chicken and pineapple seafood fried rice. We were very impressed with the presentation; the dishes were beautiful! They were tasty, but lacked any distinctive flavor that we would have liked. The chicken was not at all spicy and we hardly tasted lemongrass at all, but the two kinds of basil served on the plate added some much needed flavor. The pineapple fried rice had shrimp, baby scallops and maybe some other seafood, menu just said seafood and they were in small pieces so who knows. So in my humble opinion, the chef needs to step up the flavor a bit, but all in all, it is worth checking out. Maybe try some different menu items; the spring rolls presentation was fabulous and we wished we had ordered some.

Authentic Vietnamese Dining
Nov 2017 • Couples
This restaurant stands just blocks away from the Opera House. The property is established with glamour of good old days under French colonial rule. The menu was vast., and represented culinary cultures of this part of asia that provided us with experience to savour Vietnamese delights.
Guest service was attentive though not too sophisticated. Personally I preferred rather humane touch of hall staffs as to immaculate attention. 
Music performance that conducted as a show might require some reconsideration since musicians played too many Japanese soul ENKA numbers. Though I did appreciate such thoughtfullness, I would rather like to respect the heritage of true Vietnam.
